question: Where was the stethoscope INVENTED?

youtube.title: Who invented the stethoscope? A shy doctor and a sheet of paper 🩺
youtube.description:
Germany, England or the third one? Two centuries ago doctors listened to a heart by pressing an ear to the chest. One young physician, embarrassed in front of a female patient, rolled a sheet of paper into a tube — and heard the heartbeat more clearly than ever. He named it from the Greek, wrote the book, and died of the very disease his tube diagnosed best.
Guess before the map lights up, then see the hospital, the old method wiped away, and the two dates that made the instrument.
Which did you pick?

v04.text: France. In 1816, at the Necker Hospital in Paris, René Laennec rolled a sheet of paper into a tube.

v05.text: Doctors pressed an ear to the chest. With a young woman patient Laennec found that awkward; the tube carried her heartbeat clearly.

v06.text: He named it the stethoscope, from the Greek for chest and look, and published his findings in 1819.

v07.text: Laennec died at 45 of tuberculosis, the disease his own instrument diagnosed best.

facts.text: a rolled sheet of paper · Paris

research.topic: The stethoscope was invented in France: René Théophile Hyacinthe Laennec, Necker Hospital, Paris, 1816 — a rolled paper cylinder used to hear a young woman's heart; named from Greek stethos (chest) + skopein (to look/examine); published in 'De l'auscultation médiate' (1819); Laennec died of tuberculosis in 1826 aged 45.

myths.myth: The stethoscope was a British or German invention like much of 19th-century medical kit.
myths.reality: Laennec, a French physician, invented it in Paris in 1816 and published it in 1819.

landscape.our_gap: Feed clips tell the Laennec anecdote as a talking head; nobody pins the hospital, wipes the ear-to-chest method off the screen and splits the two dates on a moving map.
